SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl vowed to trample Muhammad's neck and rub his face in dust if he saw him prostrating, prompting the verse that humanity transgresses.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو جهل هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم فقيل نعم فقال واللات والعزى لئن رأيته يفعل لأطأن على رقبته

BURSEVI:v10p364/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p364/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p364/r9.claim: The human being crosses limits and grows arrogant toward his Lord; the verse identifies what is being rebuked and restrained.
BURSEVI:v10p364/r9.anchor: أي يتجاوز الحد ويستكبر على ربه بيان للمردوع

QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.claim: God taught the Prophet what he had not known and granted knowledge so that, before he was firmly established in abiding, he would not claim independent perfection and transgress through selfhood; self-sufficiency produces transgression.
QASHANI:96:3-8/r3.anchor: لم يكن له علم فعلمه بعلمه ووهب له صفة عالميته لئلا يرى ذاته موصوفة بصفة الكمال فيطغى

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r9.claim: A person transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient and becomes blind to his need; if he witnesses his need rather than admiring himself, he does not transgress.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r9.anchor: فإذا لم يكن معجبا بنفسه ، وكان مشاهدا لمحل افتقاره - لم يكن طاغيا

SULAMI:v2p407#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r1.claim: Seeing oneself as wealthy breeds tyranny and arrogance through pride.
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : رؤية الغنى تورث الطغيان والبطر ، لأنه يورث الفخر

SULAMI:v2p407#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r2.claim: Knowledge and wealth each produce tyranny; asceticism protects from tyranny in worship, and persistent hunger helps reach asceticism by cutting desire for sin.
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r2.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : في الدنيا طغيانان : طغيان العلم ، وطغيان المال

SULAMI:v2p407#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r3.claim: Wealth harms one whose proper state is poverty; feeling self-sufficient through wealth makes him insolent toward the Enricher.
SULAMI:v2p407#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : طغيان الغني لمن لا يصلح له إلا الفقر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says two people are insatiable—the scholar and the worldly person; they differ because the scholar gains God's approval while the worldly person persists in transgression, linking these verses with the verse about learned fear.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا ، ولا يستويان ، فاما صاحب العلم فيزداد رضا الرحمن

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra recounts Abu Jahl threatening to trample Muhammad while he prayed, then retreating when he saw a fiery trench and angels; the Prophet says angels would have seized him, and the narrator is unsure whether the verse was named in the report.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي حازم ، عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفى محمد وجهه بين اظهركم ؟ قالوا : نعم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r2.claim: Abdullah repeats that the scholar and worldly seeker are both insatiable but unequal, reciting the verses about transgression and learned fear.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r2.anchor: عن عون قال : قال عبد الله : منهومان لا يشبعان ، صاحب العلم وصاحب الدنيا ، ولا يستويان

TUSTARI:96:6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:96:6/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:96:6/r1.claim: Seeing oneself as wealthy breeds self-sufficiency, which in turn breeds transgression.
TUSTARI:96:6/r1.anchor: رؤية الغنى تورث الاستغناء، والاستغناء يورث الطغيان.

TUSTARI:96:6/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:96:6/r2.speaker: الحسن
TUSTARI:96:6/r2.claim: Hasan says the servant denied worldly goods has poor insight if he fails to recognize this as God's regard, while the one granted abundance has poor insight if he does not fear it may be divine guile.
TUSTARI:96:6/r2.anchor: لقد قصر نظر عبد زويت عنه الدنيا، ثم لم يعلم أن ذلك نظر من الله،

TUSTARI:96:6/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:96:6/r3.speaker: الحسن
TUSTARI:96:6/r3.claim: Hasan says God has never expanded worldly life for a servant without that servant becoming transgressive, whoever he may be.
TUSTARI:96:6/r3.anchor: ثم قال: والله ما بسطت الدنيا لعبد إلا طغى كائنا من كان،

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r7.claim: Kalla is a rebuke and invalidation; appearing before any obvious target indicates that the intended target follows, namely the one who forbids a servant from praying.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.claim: Kalla normally follows the speech it rejects, but here it opens the sentence because the following statement is what deserves repudiation; Imru al-Qays offers a similar initial negative particle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r1.anchor: وحق { كلا } أن تقع بعد كلام لإبطاله والزجر عن مضمونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.claim: The accounts can be reconciled: the passage beginning at 96:9 directly concerns Abu Jahl, while the statement about human transgression through 96:8 prepares for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r4.anchor: ووجه الجمع بين الروايتين : أن النازل في أبي جهل بعضه مقصود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.claim: Exegetes disagree whether these verses followed the first five immediately; prayer's mention seems problematic if obligatory prayer began at the Night Journey years later. Some posit intervening revelation and later attachment, while others deny this was the first revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p442/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في أن هذه الآيات إلى آخر السورة نزلت عقب الخمس الآيات الماضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p443/r7.claim: The statement that the human transgresses when he considers himself self-sufficient introduces the account of the man who forbids prayer and its continuation through the command not to obey him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r9.claim: Kalla refutes Abu Jahl's words and actions; it can also mean “indeed,” affirming what follows.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r9.anchor:
وكلا:
هي رد على أقوال أبي جهل وأفعاله، ويتجه أن تكون بمعنى: حقا،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r10.claim: Transgression means exceeding proper limits; wealth leads to transgression unless God protects a person.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r10.anchor: والطغيان: تجاوز الحدود الجميلة، والغني: مطغ إلا من عصم الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#4/r1.claim: Kalla means 'certainly'; the human who becomes insolent is Abu Jahl, who grew proud and boastful in clothing, mounts and food after gaining wealth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#4/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل كلا لا يعلم أن الله علمه ثم استأنف فقال تعالى إن الإنسان ليطغى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r1.claim: A person becomes exultant and transgressive upon seeing himself wealthy; he returns to God, who will question how wealth was acquired and spent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن الإنسان أنه ذو فرح وأشر وبطر وطغيان، إذا رأى نفسه قد استغنى وكثر ماله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r2.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says that the knowledge-seeker and worldly seeker are insatiable, but the former grows in the Merciful's approval while the latter persists in transgression; he recited 35:28.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r2.anchor: عن عون قال: قال عبد الله: منهومان لا يشبعان، صاحب العلم وصاحب الدنيا، ولا يستويان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r3.claim: A version raised to the Prophet says that the knowledge-seeker and worldly seeker are two insatiable people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p437#2/r3.anchor: وقد روي هذا مرفوعا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "منهومان لا يشبعان: طالب علم، وطالب دنيا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl swearing to trample Muhammad while he prayed; as he approached he recoiled, describing a trench of fire, terror, and wings. The Prophet says angels would have snatched him limb by limb; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation context was part of Abu Hurayra's report. Ibn Kathir says Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit it through Mu'tamir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قالوا: نعم. قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته يصلي

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#2/r1.claim: A human being transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#2/r1.anchor: {إن الإنسان ليطغى * أن رآه استغنى} أي يطغى أن رأى نفسه استغنى.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has seventeen verses.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r8.claim: Ṭughyān means exceeding the limits in disobedience.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r1.claim: Kalla rebukes the person who disbelieves in God's favor through tyranny, though the object is omitted because context supplies it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r1.anchor: ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه ، وإن لم يذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r2.claim: An ra'ahu means “he sees himself”; cognition verbs can take both pronouns, so the seeing is knowing rather than sight.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r2.anchor: ومعنى الرؤية : العلم ، ولو كانت بمعنى الإبصار لامتنع في فعلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r3.claim: Istaghna is the second object of the seeing verb.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r6.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Abu Jahl, including the one who forbids prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r6.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في أبي جهل . وكذلك { أرأيت الذي ينهى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r7.speaker: أبو جهل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r7.claim: Abu Jahl demanded gold and silver mountains so people could grow rich, overstep, abandon their religion, and follow Muhammad; Gabriel offered this, but the Prophet declined.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p783/r7.anchor: فاجعل لنا جبال مكة فضة وذهبا ، لعلنا نأخذ منها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p785/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p785/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p785/r1.claim: A report promises the reward of reciting all the short Meccan suras to whoever recites al-Alaq.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p785/r1.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r1.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r1.claim: Kalla here may be a repudiation and denial.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r1.anchor: في ( كلا ) ها هنا وجهان : أحدهما : أنه رد وتكذيب , قاله الفراء .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم السجستاني
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r2.claim: Alternatively, kalla means except, as in Kalla sawfa ya'lamun.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه بمعنى إلا , وكذلك { كلا سوف يعلمون } , قاله أبو حاتم السجستاني .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r3.claim: One gloss of yatgha is that a person becomes insolent and exultant.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r4.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r4.claim: Another gloss of yatgha is rising from one rank to another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r4.anchor: الثالث : ليرتفع من منزلة إلى منزلة , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r5.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r5.claim: A further gloss of yatgha is exceeding one's proper bounds, as water did when it overflowed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p306/r5.anchor: الرابع : ليتجاوزه قدره , ومنه قوله تعالى { إنا لما طغى الماء } قاله ابن شجرة .

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349/r1.claim: “No indeed” rebukes the person who responds to God's favor with transgression; although he is not named, the context identifies him. The verse through the end of the surah was revealed about Abu Jahl.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349/r1.anchor: ﴿ كلا ﴾ ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه وان لم يذكر

NAHHAS:v5p261/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r10.claim: The pause after this statement is complete throughout the Qur'an; reflecting on human creation reveals God's oneness and lack of a peer.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r10.anchor: تمام في جميع القرآن قال المعنى ليس يجب أن يدعو التفكر فيما بينه الله من خلقكم

NAHHAS:v5p261/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r11.claim: The form yaṭghā is faʿala yafʿalu because it contains the guttural ghayn.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r11.anchor: ( إن الإنسان ليطغى ) جاء على فعل يفعل لأن فيه الغين

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r1.claim: One report says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl; another says the entire sura came when he barred the Prophet from prayer, which would make it later than the first revelations.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى } إلى آخر السورة. قيل: إنه نزل في أبي جهل.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r2.claim: The first five verses may have come first and the remainder later about Abu Jahl, with God ordering their placement together, just as the last-revealed al-Baqara 2:281 was joined to much earlier verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون خمس آيات من أولها أول ما نزلت، ثم نزلت البقية في شأن أبي جهل،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r3.claim: Kalla here means indeed, since no preceding statement calls for a literal no; the human is Abu Jahl, and transgression is exceeding the limit in disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:6-7/r3.anchor: و«كلا» بمعنى حقا إذ ليس قبله شيء. والإنسان هنا أبو جهل. والطغيان: مجاوزة الحد

QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r1.claim: Humanity should recognize and thank God for creating, teaching, and honoring it, yet instead it deviates from that obligation.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r1.anchor: من مقتضيات تلك الحقيقة : حقيقة أن الله هو الذي خلق .

QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r2.claim: God is also the source who gave the transgressor wealth, as well as his creation, honor, and knowledge.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:6/r2.anchor: كما أنه هو الذي خلقه وأكرمه وعلمه

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r1.claim: Most exegetes identify the transgressing human as Abu Jahl; some say the whole surah concerns him, others only from the prohibition scene onward.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أن المراد من الإنسان ههنا إنسان واحد وهو أبو جهل

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.claim: While the Prophet prayed, Abu Jahl threatened him; his boast about having the largest gathering occasioned the summons of his assembly and the zabaniya, who would seize him if he summoned them.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r3.claim: Reminding a human made from a clot of his origin should prevent arrogance; Abu Jahl instead grew more defiant through wealth and Meccan leadership.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r3.anchor: لما عرفه أنه مخلوق من علق فلا يليق به التكبر

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r4.claim: Abu Jahl reportedly said no one in Mecca was more honored than he; the commentator conjectures this answered the description of God as most generous.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r4.anchor: ويروى أنه قال : ليس بمكة أكرم مني

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r5.claim: Some deny that the whole surah was among the earliest revelations; others say the first five verses came first and the rest later about Abu Jahl, then God ordered them joined.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r5.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون خمس آيات من أول السورة نزلت أولا

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r6.claim: As an example of later material being joined to earlier revelation, commentators call 2:281 the last-revealed verse although it was attached to older material.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r6.anchor: { واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله }

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r7.claim: Although reports make Abu Jahl the more apparent referent, the surface context more closely supports humanity generally: despite creation and blessings, people transgress through sin and appetite, and face judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r7.anchor: القول الأول وإن كان أظهر بحسب الروايات ، إلا أن هذا القول أقرب بحسب الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r1.claim: Kalla is a rebuke restraining the human who repays God's favor with transgression, though the object of rebuke is implicit in context.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r1.anchor: أنه ردع وزجر لمن كفر بنعمة الله بطغيانه

RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r2.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r2.claim: Kalla means the human fails to recognize that God created him from a clot and taught him after ignorance, because wealth absorbs him in worldly love.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل : كلا لا يعلم الإنسان إن الله هو الذي خلقه من العلقة

RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r3.speaker: الجرجاني صاحب النظم
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r3.claim: Al-Jurjani reads kalla as an affirmative ‘indeed,’ since nothing before or after it supplies an object for a rebuttal; he compares its use in 74:32.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r3.anchor: ذكر الجرجاني صاحب النظم أن { كلا } ههنا بمعنى حقا

RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r4.claim: Transgression means arrogance and rebellion; love of wealth, status, abundance, and power is the root cause of heedlessness toward the surah's proofs of divine unity, power, and wisdom.

RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r5.claim: The emphatic lām in the prediction about Abu Jahl exceeds the wording about Pharaoh because the latter command preceded Moses' encounter, evidence, and Pharaoh's divinity claim, whereas this passage consoles Muhammad after rejection.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r5.anchor: وههنا ذكر في أبي جهل : { ليطغى } فأكده بهذه اللام

RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r6.claim: Pharaoh's unbelief remained verbal despite his power, while Abu Jahl, despite lesser standing, sought to kill and harm the Prophet; this makes the stronger emphasis fitting.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r6.anchor: فرعون مع كمال سلطته ما كان يزيد كفره على القول

RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r7.claim: Pharaoh first treated Moses well and eventually professed faith, unlike Abu Jahl, who envied Muhammad from youth and died hating him.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r7.anchor: وأما أبو جهل فكان يحسد النبي في صباه

RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r8.claim: The beloved Prophet is to the interlocutor Moses as the eye to the hand; people guard the eye more, so the warning is more emphatic here.
RAZI-FULL:v32p19/r8.anchor: الحبيب في مقابلة الكليم كاليد في مقابلة العين

STUDYQURAN:96:6/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r2.claim: The emphatic kallā rebukes people for denying and failing to thank God for creation and knowledge; rebellion includes resistance to God's teaching.
STUDYQURAN:96:6/r2.anchor: kallā) here implies that despite the

TAB:96:6/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:6/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:6/r1.claim: It is wrong for a person to receive God's gifts of sound creation, knowledge, and unmatched favor, then disbelieve and transgress against Him.
TAB:96:6/r1.anchor: ما هكذا ينبغي أن يكون الإنسان أن يُنْعِمَ عليه ربّه بتسويته خَلقه ،   وتعليمه ما لم يكن يعلم

TAB:96:6/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:6/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:6/r2.claim: The human oversteps bounds, grows arrogant toward God, and disbelieves because he sees himself as self-sufficient.
TAB:96:6/r2.anchor: إنّ الإنْسانَ لَيَطْغَى أنْ رآهُ اسْتَغْنَى ،   يقول :  إن الإنسان ليتجاوز حدّه

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.claim: These verses were revealed concerning Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, who threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r3.anchor:
هذه نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام، وكذلك: (أرأيت الذي ينهى (9) عبدا إذا صلى (10).
لأن أبا جهل قال: إن رأيت محمدا يصلي توطأت عنقه.

TABRISI:96:2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r11.claim: Grammatically, the hidden subject of ra'ahu returns to the hidden subject of yatgha, and its object pronoun also refers to that subject; this is allowed with verbs of knowing because their predicate is the subject itself, unlike ordinary verbs that need nafsi.
TABRISI:96:2/r11.anchor: الضمير المستكن في رآه عائد إلى الضمير المستكن في يطغى والهاء في رآه عائد إلى الضمير

TABRISI:96:2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r12.claim: The phrase ra'ahu istaghna is a second object of ra'ahu, with the implied sense that he sees himself self-sufficient.

TABRISI:96:3-10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:3-10/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:3-10/r11.claim: Kalla here means truly; a human exceeds bounds, grows proud against his Lord, and transgresses his proper limit.
TABRISI:96:3-10/r11.anchor: أي يتجاوز حد ويستكبر على ربه ويعدو طوره

THALABI:v10p245/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p245/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p245/r5.claim: The human transgresses by exceeding his limits and becoming arrogant toward his Lord when he sees himself self-sufficient.
THALABI:v10p245/r5.anchor: كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى ليتجاوز حده ويستكبر على ربه أن رآه استغنى

THALABI:v10p245/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p245/r6.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v10p245/r6.claim: He explains self-sufficiency as rising in status through clothing, food, and similar things.
THALABI:v10p245/r6.anchor: قال الكلبي: يرتفع من منزلة إلى منزلة في اللباس والطعام وغيرهما

THALABI:v10p245/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p245/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p245/r7.claim: The Prophet sought refuge from poverty that makes one forgetful and wealth that makes one transgress.
THALABI:v10p245/r7.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r1.claim: This verse and the remainder of the sūra were revealed concerning Abū Jahl.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r1.anchor: قالوا: نزلت هذه الآية وما بعدها إلى آخر السورة في أبي جهل (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r2.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says Abū Jahl does not believe that God taught Muḥammad the revelation and prophethood he brought.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r2.anchor: قال عطاء: لا يصدق أبو جهل أن الله تعالى علم محمدا هذا الذي جاء به من النبوة (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r3.claim: Muqātil takes kallā as a correction: the human does not realize that God taught him what he did not know.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كلا لا يعلم الإنسان إن الله علمه ما لم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r1.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r1.claim: Some read kallā as an affirmative “indeed,” since neither preceding nor following material calls for a rejection; they compare its use in 74:32.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r1.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: زعم بعضهم أن (كلا) هاهنا بمعنى حقا؛ لأنه ليس قبله ولا بعده شيء تكون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r2.claim: “The human” is Abū Jahl; his transgression was that when wealthy he upgraded his clothes, mount, food, and drink. Al-Kalbī similarly describes him rising in status through dress and food.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p171#2/r2.anchor: {إن الإنسان} يعني أبا جهل. [[ليطغى]] قال مقاتل: كلا إذا أصاب مالا زاد في ثيابه، ومركبه

WAHIDI-QT:96:6/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:6/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:6/r1.claim: “Kalla” means truly; a person transgresses his limits and grows arrogant toward his Lord.
WAHIDI-QT:96:6/r1.anchor: { كلا } حقا { إن الإنسان ليطغى } ليتجاوز حده ويستكبر على ربه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r7.claim: The particle rebukes emphatically: the human oversteps and grows arrogant toward his Lord.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r7.anchor: كلا } حقا { إن الإنسان ليطغى } ليتجاوز ويستكبر على ربه.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r9.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r9.claim: Elmalılı says the later passage was revealed much later because of Abu Jahl; Bukhari and Tirmidhi relate Ibn Abbas's report that he threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him praying at the Kaaba.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r9.anchor: Ezcümle Buhârî ve Tirmizî’de İbn Abbas’tan rivayet edildiği üzere

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r10.claim: One interpretation takes the warning as addressed first to Abu Jahl, attached to the relative phrase, though this leaves the opening of the surah disconnected from it.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r10.anchor: bu surette رَبِّكَ ٱلَّذِى sûrenin evveline merbut olmamış, Ebû Cehil’in sözünü reddederek ona tevcîh-i hitab etmiş oluyor

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r11.claim: Others take kalla as affirmative “indeed” rather than rebuke, keeping the address directed to the Prophet.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r11.anchor: Onun için bazıları da burada “kellâ” zecr için değil

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r12.claim: Elmalılı prefers the Prophet as the initial addressee and takes kalla as a warning not to stop repeating the command to read, preserving the passage's coherence.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r12.anchor: nazmın insicâmı itibariyle de muvâfık olduğundan mâna şu olmak lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r13.claim: The warning tells Muhammad not to stop reading: humans surely transgress when they see themselves as self-sufficient, as Abu Jahl exemplifies.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r13.anchor: çünkü insan muhakkak tuğyan eder azar, haddini aşar, hakka karşı gelir

ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r15.claim: Although the address is to the Prophet, the chief aim is to warn the self-sufficient transgressors, illustrated by the arrogant unbeliever who occasioned the revelation.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#3/r15.anchor: Bununla beraber asıl murad istiğnâ ve tuğyan edenlere inzardır. Onun için sebeb-i nüzul olan müstağnî azgının tuğyânı bir misâl

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r1.speaker: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r1.claim: Most exegetes identify the criticized human as Abu Jahl; a report says he vowed to trample Muhammad while praying, but retreated when confronted by a fiery barrier and winged beings, and the Prophet said angels would have seized him; the event occasioned 96:6-19.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r1.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu 6. âyette eleştirilen “insan” ile bilhassa İslâm’ın en azılı düşmanlarından olan Ebû Cehil’in kastedildiğini belirtirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r2.claim: Beyond the occasion, the passage criticizes people in every age who forget God in life's struggle, rely only on themselves, and claim to need no divine help.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r2.anchor: hangi devirde olursa olsun insanın hayat mücadelesinde Allah’ı unutup yalnız kendine güvenmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r3.claim: Kallā is a negative particle indicating that what follows should not happen; here it rebukes arrogant ingratitude, self-sufficiency, and turning from truth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r3.anchor: kellâ kelimesi olumsuzluk edatı olup devamında kendisinden sonra anlatılanların aslında olmaması gerektiğini ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r4.claim: Humans are weak and depend on God and society; God owns and can remove all resources, so boasting, disobedience, superiority, and claiming control of one's fate reflect ignorance, weak faith, and lack of insight.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:6/r4.anchor: İnsanların ellerinde bulunan bütün imkânların gerçek sahibi ise kendileri değil

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r1.claim: Ṭaġā literally means rising, surging, or overflowing; the Quran uses it of floodwater, the Thamūd catastrophe, and an unrestrained gaze.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Ṭaġā bedeutet eigentlich „ansteigen, aufwallen, über die Ufer treten“

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r2.claim: From early Meccan times the verb also describes human disobedience, conventionally translated as rebellion or arrogance, plausibly developed from crossing the proper limit.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Ansonsten charakterisiert das Verb bereits in frühmekkanischer Zeit den menschlichen Ungehorsam gegenüber Gott

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Luxenberg
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r3.claim: Luxenberg suggests the moral sense may reflect Aramaic ṭʿā, but the author favors straying from right belief over Luxenberg's proposed sense of forgetting and rejects his claim that ṭaġā is not an Arabic root.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Mit Luxenberg (Luxenberg 2000, 318 f.) wäre allerdings zu erwägen

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r4.claim: Even if Syriac influenced the moral use, speakers could understand both senses through the shared idea of exceeding the proper measure, preserving the traditional translation rebellious.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:6:anmerkung/r4.anchor: bereits in koranischer Zeit könnten Sprecher des Arabischen beide Gebrauchsweisen von ṭaġā („ansteigen, aufwallen“ einerseits, „aufsässig sein“ andererseits) als Ausprägungen einer gemeinsamen Grundbedeutung „das rechte Maß überschreiten“ interpretiert haben

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r1.claim: The Quraysh reject guidance arrogantly because wealth makes them feel self-sufficient and indifferent to God; their stated objections disguise this real motive and their love of the world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p388/r1.anchor: self-sufficient from God and their love for this world

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r2.claim: The passage descended after a period concerning Abu Jahl, who opposed the Messenger and barred him from praying at the mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r2.anchor: نزلت بعد مدة في أبي جهل، ناصب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العداوة، ونهاه عن الصلاة في المسجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r6.claim: Kalla rebukes the one who disbelieves in God's favor through transgression, although no earlier mention names him; the discourse makes him understood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r6.anchor: كلا: ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه، وإن لم يتقدم ذكره لدلالة الكلام عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r7.claim: Yatgha means to exceed the proper limit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p508/r7.anchor: إن الإنسان ليطغى: أي يجاوز الحد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes humankind for answering God's great blessings with ingratitude and transgression; the preceding passage makes the rebuke's object understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r1.anchor: ردع لمن كفر من جنس الإنسان بنعمة الله تعالى عليه بطغيانه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r2.claim: Yatghā means to exceed bounds in sin, follow the soul's desire, and grow arrogant toward God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r2.anchor: ليتجاوز والحد في المعصية واتباع هوى النفس ويستكبر على ربه عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi takes yatghā as rising from one social level to another in clothing, food, and similar things; al-Alusi rejects this as unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي أي ليرتفع عن منزلة إلى منزله في اللباس والطعام وغيرهما وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r4.claim: Some supply an unstated command to give thanks for the blessings after what God taught, explaining how the human then transgressed and disbelieved.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r4.anchor: وقدر بعضهم بعد قوله تعالى ما لم يعلم ليشكر تلك النعم الجليلة فطغى وكفر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r5.claim: Some read kallā as an emphatic indeed, since no explicit object for rebuke or restraint seems to precede it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r5.anchor: وقيل كلا بمعنى حقا لعدم ما يتوجه إليه الردع والزجر ظاهرا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r6.claim: The final passage is reported to have been revealed about Abu Jahl after the earlier verses, but its intended human remains humankind generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p182/r6.anchor: قيل نزل في أبي جهل بعد زمان من نزول الآيات السابقة وهو الظاهر ومع نزوله في ذلك اللعين المراد بالإنسان الجنس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r5.claim: Kalla means truly; humanity surely exceeds its bounds and grows arrogant toward its Lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479#2/r5.anchor: حقا {إن الإنسان ليطغى} ليتجاوز حده ويستكبر على ربه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r4.claim: كلا rebukes the one who rejects God's favor through transgression; a person transgresses when he sees himself as self-sufficient.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r4.anchor: كلا } ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله بطغيانه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.claim: The warning turns to the human tendency to become arrogant about knowledge and status among created beings.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r4.anchor: ويمضي البيان القرآني، في الردع المحذر مما يتعرض له الإنسان من غرور بعلمه ومكانه بين المحلوقات

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r5.claim: طغيان means exceeding bounds, especially the tyranny of despots; استغناء is the opposite of need, and كلا rebukes and restrains.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r5.anchor: الطغيان تجاوز الحد، وأكثر ما يستعمل في جبروت العتاة المستبدين. والاستغناء ضد الاحتياج

BINTSHATI:v2p24/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r6.claim: Some interpreters take كلا to mean indeed, arguing that neither preceding nor following material provides anything for a rebuke to address.
BINTSHATI:v2p24/r6.anchor: من المفسرين من تأولها بمعنى "حقاً" لأنه ليس قبلها ولا بعدها شيء يتوجه إليه الردع

BINTSHATI:v2p25/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r1.claim: She rejects reading كلا as merely indeed: it directly precedes human transgression, and the following verses contain ample warning and rebuke.
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r1.anchor: فالكلمة متلوة مباشرة بطغيان الإنسان، والآيات بعدها حافلة بما يتوجه إليه الردع والنذير

BINTSHATI:v2p25/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r2.claim: The cause is not absorption in money or status; the text says the human imagines himself independent of his Creator and is lured by acquired knowledge into overstepping his place.
BINTSHATI:v2p25/r2.anchor: وليس الطغيان عن استغراق في حب المال والجاه كما تأوله بعض المفسرين

BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.claim: Al-Razi’s second solution reads الإنسان generically: despite creation and blessings, people transgress, forget their return, and forbid worship when they should follow guidance and enjoin piety.
BINTSHATI:v2p27/r2.anchor: أن تحمل الآيات على عموم لفظها في الظاهر، وهو أن الإنسان، جملة الإنسان، خلقه الله من علق

DURR:96:6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:6/r1.claim: Ibn Masud says knowledge and worldly pursuit are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge brings divine approval, while pursuit of the world deepens transgression.
DURR:96:6/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

DURR:96:6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:6/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl threatening to trample Muhammad if he saw him praying at the Kaaba; the Prophet warns that angels would seize him openly.
DURR:96:6/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن رأيت محمداً يصلي عند الكعبة لأطأن عنقه

DURR:96:6/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r5.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
DURR:96:6/r5.claim: Al-Abbas reports Abu Jahl vowed to tread on Muhammad’s neck; when Muhammad recited the surah, Abu Jahl saw the sky blocked and Muhammad prostrated at its end.
DURR:96:6/r5.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب قال : كنت يوماً في المسجد فأقبل أبو جهل

DURR:96:6/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:96:6/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl approached Muhammad during prayer to trample him, recoiled from a fiery trench and wings, and was identified as the transgressor; the council are his people and the guards angels.
DURR:96:6/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه إلا بين أظهركم ؟ قالوا : نعم

DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.claim: He says the seeker of knowledge and seeker of worldly wealth are both insatiable but unequal: knowledge increases God's approval, while wealth-seeking deepens transgression; he cites two verses.
DURR-FULL:v8p563/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: منهومان لا يشبعان: صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا ولا يستويان

FARRA:v1p333/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p333/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p333/r1.claim: Arabic uses a direct reflexive expression with complete verbs (قتلتم أنفسكم; ظلموا أنفسهم), but defective cognition verbs take a pronoun attached to the verb (أظنني خارجا), distinguishing verbs that may be omitted from those that cannot.
FARRA:v1p333/r1.anchor: في الأفعال التامة غير ما يقولون في الناقصة

FARRA:v1p333/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p333/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p333/r2.claim: The Qurʾān says أن رآه استغنى rather than رأى نفسه; poetry can use a direct object with a complete verb, but forms such as عدمتني are not standard speech.
FARRA:v1p333/r2.anchor: أن رآه استغنى ولم يقل: رأى نفسه

BURHAN:v2p140/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p140/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p140/r5.claim: The Prophet's fear that worldly abundance and adornment will be opened to the community is associated with the human tendency to transgress when self-sufficient.
BURHAN:v2p140/r5.anchor: وقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم فى مثل الدنيا إن مما أخاف عليكم ما يفتح عليكم من زهرة الدنيا وزينتها

BURHAN:v4p315/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p315/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
BURHAN:v4p315/r3.claim: Abu Hatim says kalla is an opening particle meaning ألا; he adduces Gabriel's first five verses of al-Alaq, the pause after 96:5, and the later revelation beginning with kalla at 96:6.
BURHAN:v4p315/r3.anchor: فدل على إن الابتداء ب كلا من طريق الوحي فهي في الابتداء بمعنى ألا عنده

ITQAN:v3p196/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.claim: Repeating al-insan creates paronomasia: the first is humanity as a species, the second may be Adam, a literate person, or Idris, and the third is Abu Jahl.
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.anchor: ومثله ابن الصائغ بقوله ﴿ خلق الإنسان من علق ﴾ ثم قال ﴿ علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى

ITQAN:v2p494#3/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r5.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r5.claim: Ibn Hisham notes that the first five verses of al-ʿAlaq were the earliest revelation, then kallā opened a new statement, which challenges the rebuke-only reading.
ITQAN:v2p494#3/r5.anchor: وأيضا فإن أول ما نزل خمس آيات من أول سورة العلق ثم نزل ﴿ كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى ﴾ فجاءت في افتتاح الكلام

DAMGHANI:v1p49/r5.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r5.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r5.claim: In the passage about transgression when one sees oneself as self-sufficient, al-insān refers to Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r5.anchor: الإنسان يعني أبا جهل بن هشام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r4.claim: The human who transgresses after seeing himself as self-sufficient is identified as Abū Jahl ibn Hishām.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r3.claim: Kallā occurs 33 times in the Quran’s second part and not in its first; its rebuking and interrogative force fits the mostly Meccan second part’s creed, judgment, and resurrection themes, unlike the mostly Medinan legal material in the first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r3.anchor: كلمة (كلاّ) وردت في الجزء الثاني من القرآن الكريم 33 مرة ولم ترد أبداً في الجزء الأول، وهي كلمة ردع وزجر وقد تكون جواباً من حيث الدلالة.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r4.claim: In the opening of Al Alaq, kallā means حقاً (indeed), rather than functioning as rebuke.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p692/r4.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى (كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى) جاءت كلمة (كلا) هنا بمعنى حقاً.

ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r1.claim: The passage was revealed later concerning Abu Jahl, who opposed the Messenger and forbade him to pray in the mosque.
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r1.anchor: نزلت بعد مدة في أبي جهل ، ناصب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم العداوة ، ونهاه عن الصلاة في المسجد

ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r2.speaker: أبو جهل
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r2.claim: Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him prostrating at the Kaaba.
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r2.anchor: فروي أنه قال : لئن رأيت محمداً يسجد عند الكعبة لأطأن على عنقه

ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r3.speaker: رسول الله وأبو جهل
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r3.claim: The Messenger rebuked and threatened him; Abu Jahl retorted that Muhammad was threatening him although no one in the valley had a larger following than he did.
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r3.anchor: فيروى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رد عليه وانتهره وتوعده ، فقال أبو جهل : أيتوعدني محمد ! والله ما بالوادي أعظم نادياً مني

ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r4.speaker: أبو جهل
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r4.claim: Another report says Abu Jahl considered preventing the Prophet from praying but then refrained.
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r4.anchor: ويروى أنه هم أن يمنعه من الصلاة ، فكف عنه

ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r5.claim: كلا rebukes the one who responds to God's favor with disbelief and transgression, even though that person was not previously named.
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r5.anchor: { كلا } : ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه ، وإن لم يتقدم ذكره لدلالة الكلام عليه

ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r6.claim: The human's transgression means exceeding the bounds.
ABUHAYYAN:96:6/r6.anchor: { إن الإنسان ليطغى } : أي يجاوز الحد

ALUSI:96:6/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:6/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:6/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the human who met God’s favors with disbelief and transgression, though that target is implicit in the discourse.
ALUSI:96:6/r1.anchor: ردع لمن كفر من جنس الإنسان بنعمة الله تعالى عليه بطغيانه

ALUSI:96:6/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:6/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:6/r2.claim: The sūra’s opening recounts God’s immense favor to humanity, making kallā a rebuke for answering those favors with ingratitude.
ALUSI:96:6/r2.anchor: وذلك لأن مفتتح السورة إلى هذا المقطع يدل على عظيم منته تعالى على الإنسان فإذا قيل كلا كان ردعاً للإنسان

ALUSI:96:6/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:6/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:6/r3.claim: The human oversteps bounds through sin, following desire, and arrogance toward his Lord.
ALUSI:96:6/r3.anchor: أي ليتجاوز والحد في المعصية واتباع هوى النفس ويستكبر على ربه عز وجل

ALUSI:96:6/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:6/r4.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI:96:6/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets the phrase as rising from one social level to another in clothing, food, and similar things; al-Ālūsī dismisses this view.
ALUSI:96:6/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي أي ليرتفع عن منزلة إلى منزلة

ALUSI:96:6/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:6/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI:96:6/r5.claim: Some supply an omitted thought after verse 5: the human should have thanked God for these great favors, but instead transgressed and disbelieved.
ALUSI:96:6/r5.anchor: ليشكر تلك النعم الجليلة فطغى وكفر كلا

ALUSI:96:6/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:6/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:6/r6.claim: Some take kallā to mean “truly,” since no explicit object of rebuke seems present; the following statement then explains what is affirmed.
ALUSI:96:6/r6.anchor: وقيل كلا بمعنى حقاً لعدم ما يتوجه إليه الردع والزجر ظاهراً

ALUSI:96:6/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:6/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:6/r7.claim: The closing passage apparently was revealed about Abū Jahl after an interval from the earlier verses, but al-insān still denotes humanity generally.
ALUSI:96:6/r7.anchor: وهذا إلى آخر السورة قيل نزل في أبي جهل بعد زمان من نزول الآيات السابقة وهو الظاهر ومع نزوله في ذلك اللعين المراد بالإنسان الجنس

BAGHAWI:96:6/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:6/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:6/r2.claim: The human exceeds proper bounds and grows arrogant toward his Lord.

BAYDAWI:96:6/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:6/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:6/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the person who responds to God's favor with transgression, although that ingratitude was only implied before this point.

BIQAI:96:6/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:6/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:6/r1.claim: The rebuke tells a learned person to desist from tyranny if truly enriched; the passage turns from divine matters to the human soul and identifies the human type destined for the lowest state.
BIQAI:96:6/r1.anchor: ارتدع أيها العالم عن الطغيان إن نلت الغنى حقاً

BIQAI:96:6/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:6/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:6/r2.claim: Humans characteristically exceed proper limits, except those God protects; Biqāʿī compares this excess to the agitation of the blood humor.
BIQAI:96:6/r2.anchor: هذا النوع الذي هو نوعك ومن شأنه الأنس بنفسه

BIQAI:96:6/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:6/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:6/r3.claim: Blood is the largest and most volatile humor, so its illness is unlike disorders of the other humors, yet it can quickly be cured by a stronger, correctly applied remedy.
BIQAI:96:6/r3.anchor: كان الدم أكثر الأخلاط وأشدها هيجاناً

BIQAI:96:6/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:6/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:6/r4.claim: Knowledge commonly accompanies wealth, and a learned person's error outweighs the error of someone else.
BIQAI:96:6/r4.anchor: وكان العلم قرين الغنى في الأغلب

IBNASHUR:96:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r1.claim: Kallā rebuts and cancels; because the preceding sentence offers nothing to reject, its opening placement signals that the following statement warrants refutation, like Imruʾ al-Qays's opening negative oath.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r1.anchor: وحرف { كلاّ } ردع وإبطال ،  وليس في الجملة التي قبله ما يحتمل الإبطال والردع ،  فوجود { كلا } في أول الجملة دليل على أن المقصود بالردع

IBNASHUR:96:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR:96:6/r2.claim: Muslim transmits from Abū Hurayra through Abū Ḥāzim that Abū Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad while praying, then recoiled, describing fire, terror, and wings; the report is unsure whether the revelation detail was in his narration or reached him separately.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r2.anchor: عن أبي حازم عن أبي هريرة قال :  « قال أبو جهل :  هل يعفر محمد وجهه

IBNASHUR:96:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r4.claim: The accounts are reconciled by taking verses 9 onward as the direct passage about Abū Jahl and verses 6–8 as its preparatory introduction.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r4.anchor: ووجه الجمع بين الروايتين :  أن النازل في أبي جهل بعضه مقصود وهو ما أوله { أرأيت الذي ينهى } الخ

IBNASHUR:96:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r5.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR:96:6/r5.claim: Some saw the prayer reference as conflicting with an immediate revelation after the first five verses, since the five daily prayers were prescribed at the later Night Journey; they proposed an intervening revelation or denied this was the first sūra.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في أن هذه الآيات إلى آخر السورة نزلت عقب الخمس الآيات الماضية وجعلوا مما يناكده ذِكر الصلاة فيها

IBNASHUR:96:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr sees no chronology problem: reports indicate a first pause in revelation after the opening five verses, as also recalled at the beginning of Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā, though reports differ on its length.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r6.anchor: وأنا لا أرى مناكدة تفضي إلى هذه الحيرة والذي يستخلص من مختلف الروايات في بدء الوحي وما عقبه من الحوادث

IBNASHUR:96:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r7.speaker: السهيلي
IBNASHUR:96:6/r7.claim: Al-Suhaylī estimates the first revelation pause at two years, which Ibn ʿĀshūr regards as unlikely; its exact duration is unimportant to him, but the Prophet received non-Qurʾānic revelation from Gabriel during it.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r7.anchor: وقال السهيلي :  كانت المدة سنتين ،  وفيه بعد .  وليس تحديد مدتها بالأمر المهم

IBNASHUR:96:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says the Prophet saw Gabriel during the pause and received revelation from him that was not Qurʾān.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r8.anchor: ولكن الذي يهم هو أنا نوقن بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان في مدة فترة الوحي يرى جبريل ويتلقى منه وحياً ليس من القرآن

IBNASHUR:96:6/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r12.claim: He holds that the verses through the sūra's end followed a short pause after its opening verses, when the Prophet's prayer and the beginning of revelation became known; adjacent recited verses normally follow in revelation order absent clear contrary proof, and this remains the first-revealed sūra.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r12.anchor: فالوجه أن تكون هذه الآيات إلى بقية السورة قد نزلت بعد فترة قصيرة من نزول أول السورة حدثت فيها صلاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.claim: The general statement that humans transgress when they feel self-sufficient introduces the specific account of the prohibitor, encompassing the challenge through Abū Jahl's invitation to his assembly.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r13.anchor: فموقع قوله :  { إن الإنسان ليطغى أن رآه استغنى } موقع المقدمة لما يرد بعده من قوله :  { أرأيت الذي ينهى

IBNASHUR:96:6/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r14.claim: Al-insān is generic, conventionally encompassing most people of that time: humans tend to transgress when they feel self-sufficient, except those restrained by sound character or religion.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r14.anchor: والتعريف في { الإنسان } للجنس ،  أي من طبع الإنسان أن يطغى إذا أحس من نفسه الاستغناء ،  واللام مفيدة الاستغراق العرفي

IBNASHUR:96:6/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r15.claim: The emphatic inna and lām intensify the assertion because its surprising truth might otherwise seem doubtful to a listener.
IBNASHUR:96:6/r15.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر بحرف التأكيد ولام الابتداء لقصد زيادة تحقيقه لغرابته حتى كأنه مما يتوقع أن يشك السامع فيه

IBNASHUR:96:6/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:6/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:6/r16.claim: Ṭughyān means arrogance and pride, the disposition expressed when a person feels secure enough to overstep others.

IBNASHUR:96:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:9/r1.claim: The question about the one who prohibits prayer is the intended target of the opening rebuke and follows the general statement about human transgression.
IBNASHUR:96:9/r1.anchor: وجملة :  { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } إلى آخرها هي المقصود من الردع الذي أفاده حرف { كلاّ }

IBNATIYYA:96:6/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the passage from Kalla through the end of the sura was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r1.anchor: فهذه السورة من قوله : { كلا } إلى آخرها نزلت في أبي جهل

IBNATIYYA:96:6/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r2.claim: He identifies the tyrannical human as Abu Jahl, whose wealth and crowded gathering emboldened his hostility to Muhammad and his ban on prayer in the mosque.
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r2.anchor: وذلك أنه طغى لغناه ولكثرة من يغشى ناديه من الناس

IBNATIYYA:96:6/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r3.claim: Abu Jahl reportedly threatened to step on Muhammad’s neck if he saw him prostrating at the Kaaba.
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r3.anchor: لئن رأيت محمداً يسجد عند الكعبة لأطأن على عنقه

IBNATIYYA:96:6/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r4.speaker: أبو جهل
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r4.claim: After Muhammad rebuked and warned him, Abu Jahl boasted that no one in the valley had a larger council than he did.
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r4.anchor: أيتوعدني ، وما بالوادي أعظم ندياً مني

IBNATIYYA:96:6/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r5.claim: When Abu Jahl tried to approach Muhammad at prayer, he recoiled, saying a trench of fire, terror, and wings had intervened.
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r5.anchor: فهمَّ بأن يصل إليه ويمنعه من الصلاة ، ثم كع عنه وانصرف

IBNATIYYA:96:6/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r6.claim: The Prophet reportedly said that if Abu Jahl came near, angels would seize him in plain sight.
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r6.anchor: لو دنا مني لأخذته الملائكة عياناً

IBNATIYYA:96:6/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r7.claim: Kalla rebuts Abu Jahl’s statements and actions.
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r7.anchor: { كلا } : هي رد على أقوال أبي جهل وأفعاله

IBNATIYYA:96:6/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r8.claim: Kalla may instead mean truly, affirming what follows.
IBNATIYYA:96:6/r8.anchor: بمعنى : حقاً ، فهي تثبيت لما بعدها من القول

MUSLIM:7065/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7065/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSLIM:7065/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl threatened to trample Muhammad during prayer, then retreated at an unseen barrier; the passage is applied to Abu Jahl, and the Prophet says angels would seize him limb by limb.
MUSLIM:7065/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي حَازِمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ، قَالَ قَالَ أَبُو جَهْلٍ هَلْ يُعَفِّرُ مُحَمَّدٌ وَجْهَهُ بَيْنَ أَظْهُرِكُمْ

MUSLIM:7065/r2.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7065/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
MUSLIM:7065/r2.claim: The transmission leaves uncertain whether the revelation attribution was in Abu Hurayra's account or something that had reached him.
MUSLIM:7065/r2.anchor: لا ندري في حديث أبي هريرة أو شيء بلغه

IBNKATHIR:96:6/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:6/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:6/r1.claim: A person becomes joyful, insolent, boastful, and transgressive when he sees himself as self-sufficient and his wealth has increased.
IBNKATHIR:96:6/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن الإنسان أنه ذو فرح وأشر وبطر وطغيان ، إذا رأى نفسه قد استغنى وكثر ماله

IBNKATHIR:96:7/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:7/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:7/r1.claim: A person becomes joyful, insolent, boastful, and transgressive when he sees himself as self-sufficient and his wealth has increased.
IBNKATHIR:96:7/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن الإنسان أنه ذو فرح وأشر وبطر وطغيان ، إذا رأى نفسه قد استغنى وكثر ماله

IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says worldly and knowledge seekers are both insatiable but unequal: the learned gain God's approval, while the worldly person persists in transgression; he connects 96:6–7 with 35:28.
IBNKATHIR:96:8/r2.anchor: عن عون قال : قال عبد الله : مَنهومان لا يشبعان

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir is unsure whether Abu Hurayra's report itself says that the passage from 96:6 through the end of the sura was revealed.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r7.anchor: وأنزل الله - لا أدري في حديث أبي هريرة أم لا - :

KASHSHAF:96:6/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:6/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:6/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the person who responds to God's favor with transgression, though that unbelief is left implicit in the context.
KASHSHAF:96:6/r1.anchor: ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه ،   وإن لم يذكر لدلالة الكلام عليه

MAWARDI:96:6/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:6/r1.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI:96:6/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads kalla here as a rejection and denial.
MAWARDI:96:6/r1.anchor: في  "  كلا  "  ها هنا وجهان : أحدهما : أنه رد وتكذيب ، قاله الفراء .

MAWARDI:96:6/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:6/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم السجستاني
MAWARDI:96:6/r2.claim: Abu Hatim al-Sijistani takes kalla to mean illa, as in kalla sawfa yaʿlamun.
MAWARDI:96:6/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه بمعنى إلا ، وكذلك { كلا سوف يعلمون } ، قاله أبو حاتم السجستاني .

MAWARDI:96:6/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:6/r4.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI:96:6/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses yatgha as becoming insolent and overbearing.

MAWARDI:96:6/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:6/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:96:6/r5.claim: Al-Suddi takes it to mean rising from one station to another.
MAWARDI:96:6/r5.anchor: الثالث : ليرتفع من منزلة إلى منزلة ، قاله السدي .

MAWARDI:96:6/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:6/r6.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI:96:6/r6.claim: Ibn Shajara says it means exceeding one's limit, supported by the wording about water overflowing in 69:11.
MAWARDI:96:6/r6.anchor: الرابع : ليتجاوز قدره ، ومنه قوله تعالى { إنّا لما طَغَى الماءُ } قاله ابن شجرة .

NASAFI:96:6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:6/r1.claim: Kallā rebukes the one who responds to God's favor with unbelief and transgression; the prior context makes that person implicit.
NASAFI:96:6/r1.anchor: { كَلاَّ } ردع لمن كفر بنعمة الله عليه بطغيانه

NASAFI:96:6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:6/r2.claim: This verse, through the end of the sūra, was revealed concerning Abū Jahl.
NASAFI:96:6/r2.anchor: نزلت في أبي جهل إلى آخر السورة

QURTUBI:96:6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:6/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:6/r1.claim: One report says this verse, or the entire sura, came down about Abu Jahl when he prohibited Muhammad from praying.
QURTUBI:96:6/r1.anchor: قيل : إنه نزل في أبي جهل . وقيل : نزلت السورة كلها في أبي جهل

QURTUBI:96:6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:6/r2.claim: If the entire sura concerned Abu Jahl, it would not all be among the earliest revelations; alternatively, the first five verses came early and the rest later, then God ordered the later material joined to them, as with 2:281.
QURTUBI:96:6/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون خمس آيات من أولها أول ما نزلت ، ثم نزلت البقية في شأن أبي جهل

QURTUBI:96:6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:6/r3.claim: Kalla means truly, since nothing precedes it here.
QURTUBI:96:6/r3.anchor: و " كلا " بمعنى حقا ؛ إذ ليس قبله شيء .

QURTUBI:96:6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:6/r4.claim: The human who transgresses here is Abu Jahl.

QURTUBI:96:6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:6/r5.claim: Transgression is exceeding the limit in disobedience.

RAZI:96:6/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI:96:6/r1.claim: Most exegetes identify the human who transgresses here as one individual, Abū Jahl.
RAZI:96:6/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أن المراد من الإنسان ههنا إنسان واحد

RAZI:96:6/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r2.speaker: منهم
RAZI:96:6/r2.claim: Some say the sūra from this verse to its end was revealed about Abū Jahl.
RAZI:96:6/r2.anchor: منهم من قال : نزلت السورة من ههنا إلى آخرها

RAZI:96:6/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r3.claim: Others say the passage about Abū Jahl begins at the verse about the one who forbids a worshipper and continues to the sūra’s end.
RAZI:96:6/r3.anchor: وقيل : نزلت من قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا }

RAZI:96:6/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:96:6/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that while the Prophet prayed, Abū Jahl threatened him and boasted of his powerful council; God revealed the warning that he could summon it and God would summon the Zabāniya, who would seize him.
RAZI:96:6/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل

RAZI:96:6/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r5.claim: A report says Abū Jahl claimed no one in Mecca was more honored than he, perhaps in response to the description of the Lord as most generous.
RAZI:96:6/r5.anchor: ويروى أنه قال : ليس بمكة أكرم مني

RAZI:96:6/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r6.speaker: منهم
RAZI:96:6/r6.claim: Some deny that the whole sūra was among the earliest revelations; others say its first five verses came first and the rest later about Abū Jahl, then were joined by God’s command, as with 2:281.
RAZI:96:6/r6.anchor: ومنهم من قال : يحتمل أن يكون خمس آيات من أول السورة نزلت أولا

RAZI:96:6/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r7.claim: Although reports favor Abū Jahl, Rāzī prefers the generic human: despite creation, blessings, and enrichment, people transgress in sins and desire; the return to God warns them of judgment.

RAZI:96:6/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r8.claim: Kallā is an implied rebuke restraining whoever responds to God’s favor with transgression.
RAZI:96:6/r8.anchor: ردع وزجر لمن كفر بنعمة الله بطغيانه

RAZI:96:6/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r9.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:96:6/r9.claim: Muqātil reads kallā as denying that the human recognizes God created him from a clot and taught him after ignorance, since wealth makes him arrogant and inattentive.
RAZI:96:6/r9.anchor: قال مقاتل : كلا لا يعلم الإنسان

RAZI:96:6/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r10.speaker: الجرجاني
RAZI:96:6/r10.claim: Al-Jurjānī, author of al-Naẓm, says kallā means truly here, not a rebuttal; he makes the same reading in the oath by the moon.
RAZI:96:6/r10.anchor: ذكر الجرجاني صاحب «النظم » أن ( كلا ) ههنا بمعنى حقا

RAZI:96:6/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r11.claim: Transgression here means arrogance and rebellion.
RAZI:96:6/r11.anchor: الطغيان هو التكبر والتمرد ، وتحقيق الكلام

RAZI:96:6/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r12.claim: After establishing signs of divine unity, power, and wisdom, Rāzī identifies attachment to worldly wealth, status, prosperity, and power as the chief cause of heedlessness and blindness of heart.
RAZI:96:6/r12.anchor: هو السبب الأصلي في الغفلة عنها

RAZI:96:6/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r13.claim: The emphatic lām contrasts with the account of Pharaoh: God told Moses Pharaoh had transgressed before Moses met him or presented evidence, while this verse comforts the Prophet after a harsh rejection.

RAZI:96:6/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r14.claim: Despite Pharaoh’s power, his disbelief did not go beyond words and he would not attack Moses; Abū Jahl, despite lesser status, intended to kill and injure the Prophet.
RAZI:96:6/r14.anchor: وما كان ليتعرض لقتل موسى عليها السلام ولا لإيذائه

RAZI:96:6/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r15.claim: Pharaoh initially treated Moses well and ultimately professed faith, whereas Abū Jahl envied Muhammad from youth and died hating him.

RAZI:96:6/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r16.claim: Rāzī reports Abū Jahl’s final message to Muhammad: he died with no one more hateful to him, underscoring the contrast with Pharaoh.
RAZI:96:6/r16.anchor: وقال في آخر رمقه : بلغوا عني محمدا أني أموت

RAZI:96:6/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:6/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:96:6/r17.claim: The greater emphasis also honors Muhammad: the beloved Prophet stands to Moses the interlocutor as the eye to the hand, and a person guards the eye more carefully.
RAZI:96:6/r17.anchor: الحبيب في مقابلة الكليم كاليد في مقابلة العين
